body:
WHAT
The scheduler checks every 30 seconds whether a job is due. A due job fires only when the session is idle (no turn is running). If the session is busy, the job is left in place and re-checked on the next tick, so it lands at the start of a fresh turn, never in the middle of one.

WHY
A prompt injected into a running turn would interleave with the agent's own work and corrupt the conversation.

WHERE
engine/core/src/scheduling/cron.ts — `CronScheduler.tick()` (`if (!idle) continue;`), `isDue()`, `fireKey()` / `lastFireKey` (so one occurrence fires once), `const TICK_MS`; the idle predicate is supplied in engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts `constructor` as `isIdle: () => !this.session.isBusy()` and the fired prompt goes through `enqueue` (slash command or `user_message`).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With a controllable `isIdle` returning false and a matching minute, tick() calls enqueue zero times and list() still contains the job.
2. Flip isIdle to true and tick() again within the same minute; enqueue is called exactly once with the job's prompt and source 'cron'.
3. With isIdle true, two tick() calls in the same matching minute enqueue only once (lastFireKey dedupes the occurrence).
4. A wakeup job (scheduleWakeup) whose fireAt has passed is also held while busy and fires on the first idle tick, then is removed.
5. Engine-level: while a FakeProvider turn is in progress (session.isBusy() true), a scheduler tick enqueues nothing; after the turn finishes the next tick starts a new user turn.
